A1.justification: Both 36-page PDFs describe the same PRISM research and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G. Material moved between the appendices and main text can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantitative and qualitative generation and inversion experiments, including benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original experimental results, including Tables 1–10, qualitative demonstrations and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1 and Appendix G retain the same prompt refinement, parallel search, judging and candidate re-evaluation procedures. Multi-concept generation and prompt distillation already appeared in v2 Appendix C.3.

E1.justification: Both versions retain DreamBooth personalization, Wikiart style generation with PartiPrompts, DiffusionDB inversion and the same additional application examples. Applications presented in v3 Section 4.5 were already covered in v2.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Textual Inversion, CLIP-Interrogator, BLIP-2 and PEZ, with Liu et al. (2024) in image inversion. The GPT-4V zero-shot and appendix Idea2Img comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The data splits, 100-image inversion sample, metrics, model choices and prompt-length constraints are unchanged. Both report personalization with N=10, K=4 and inversion with N=6, K=5, using the same image-generation counts.

E4.justification: The studies of stream/iteration budgets, model choices, judge selection, re-evaluation and prompt length are retained. The application demonstrations moved from Appendix C.3 provide the same case-study evidence.

E5.justification: Run/seed disclosure and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. No confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced, and the existing judge-score distribution plots are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical entries; for example, Table 2 reports PRISM's SDXL-Turbo CLIP-I as 0.776 in both versions. Matched qualitative examples and ablation plots preserve the same results despite relocation and resizing.

T1.justification: The formal problem definition, expected similarity score and optimization objective in Equation (1) are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of automatically producing interpretable, editable and transferable prompts using black-box T2I access. Promoting existing applications into the main text does not expand these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of transferability, prompt readability and VLM judging are retained. Appendix E preserves the limitations concerning fine details, compositionality, CLIP-T alignment, instance-dependent budgets, cost, latency and potential misuse.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A's anonymous demo-code link is replaced by a project-page code-access link in v3's abstract. This revises the reported access route; implementation settings and the full system prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix F and the references retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the distinctions from Idea2Img and Liu et al. (2024).

P1.justification: Limited wording and author/affiliation edits accompany moving Appendix C.3 into Section 4.5, renamed Additional Applications. Ethic Statement becomes Broader Impact Statement, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting changes typography, text width, table sizing and figure placement throughout the main text and appendices. v2 Figures 17–18 become main-text Figures 10–11, and numerous retained displays are resized, relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves navigation and discoverability by grouping the existing application demonstrations in Section 4.5 and placing updated code-access information in the abstract. These are limited presentation and accessibility gains; the scientific method, evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
